02 / The problem

The last mile costs more than the whole route

Terrain

Mountains, canyons and rivers: the detour takes hours instead of minutes.

Weather

Fog, snow and mud close the road for days at a time.

Remoteness

Sites without roads are supplied by helicopter or all-terrain vehicle.

Cost

A dedicated vehicle run for 20 kg of cargo is expensive and slow.

02 / 08
03 / Architecture

Three layers of the delivery system

The drone flies the run, the dock services it without a person, and the platform plans routes and keeps track of the cargo. All three layers are supplied and configured as one solution.

Cargo drone

Up to 30 kg of payload, case or winch, operation in rain and wind.

Docking station

Automatic landing, charging and preparation for the next run without an operator.

Platform

Routes, dispatch, statuses and reports for every run.

03 / 08
04 / Autonomy

Docking stations:
scheduled runs 24/7

01No pilot required: take-off, landing, charging and data offload all run to schedule.
02Climate protection: battery heating and cooling, IP55+ ingress rating, operation from −20 °C to +50 °C.
03Remote control: runs are managed from a central office anywhere in the world.
04Mobile option: a pickup-mounted station deploys at a new site in minutes.
04 / 08
05 / Routes

BVLOS routes
and flight safety

01Beyond visual line of sight: the route follows terrain and altitudes, not a straight line on the map.
02Corridor check: obstacles, restricted zones and alternate pads are verified before departure.
03Cargo monitoring in flight: weight, sling position and swing are visible to the operator in real time.
04Contingency scenarios: return to the pad or land at a backup point on failure or low battery.
05 / 08
06 / Management

Fleet management
and ERP integration

01One dispatch screen: every aircraft, pad and run in a single window.
02Request queue: a delivery order becomes a run automatically — by priority, weight and departure window.
03ERP/WMS integration: run statuses flow back into the client's system over an API.
04Reporting: flight hours, kilograms delivered and cost per run for every route.

Where drone delivery pays off first

Construction and industrial sites

Tools, spare parts and concrete samples between sections — past the access gate and the traffic.

Healthcare and remote settlements

Samples, vaccines and medicines to mountain areas cut off by mud and snow.

Ports and energy

Delivery to vessels, rigs and substations without a boat or special transport.
